identity.name: Islamic State
alt_names: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
Islamic State of Iraq and Syria

land.text: Raqqa, 'IS controlled Raqqa from 2013' (Islamic State page); Raqqa had been outside the Syrian government's hands

predecessors.note: IS grew out of the Islamic State of Iraq (declared October 2006) and announced its expansion into Syria in April 2013. Its first Iraqi land (Anbar, from 30 December 2013) came from republic-of-iraq.

land.text: Anbar, Nineveh, Salah ad-Din and western Kirkuk, retaken by December 2017 ('no territory in Iraq')

successors.note: Mosul 10 July 2017, Tal Afar August, Hawija October, Al-Qaim and Rawa 17 November; Abadi announced the end of the war on 9 December 2017.

land.text: Raqqa governorate and the Euphrates east bank to Hajin and Baghuz, taken by the SDF (Raqqa 17 October 2017; Hajin 14 December 2018; Baghuz 23 March 2019)

successors.note: The SDF; the slug is that of the Autonomous Administration dossier written by this batch, which mirrors the ledger events (Kobani, Tell Abyad, al-Hawl, Tishrin, Shaddadi, Manbij, Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor east).

land.text: Deir ez-Zor and the Euphrates west bank, Mayadin and Abu Kamal retaken by the Syrian and Iraqi armies in 2017; the Palmyra desert (March 2016, March 2017)

successors.note: DZ page: "ISIL lost Al-Qa'im and Abu Kamal to the Iraqi and Syrian Army"; Palmyra on 27 March 2016 and 2 March 2017.

land.text: Jarabulus (24 August 2016) and al-Bab (23 February 2017), taken by Turkish-backed rebels in Operation Euphrates Shield

successors.note: The republic-of-turkey dossier draws the whole Euphrates Shield area as its occupation from 2016-08.

capitals.name: Raqqa
capitals.note: 'Raqqa, Syria, was the de facto capital from 2014, and the group's headquarters there ran from 2013 to 2017'; lost to the SDF on 17 October 2017.

capitals.name: Abu Kamal (Albukamal)
capitals.note: The Islamic State page lists Abu Kamal, Al-Qa'im, Mayadin and Hajin as headquarters in October-December 2017 without saying which was the seat; Abu Kamal is the researcher's choice. After March 2019 the page puts the headquarters in Idlib Governorate (insurgency, no territory).

rulers.name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
rulers.title: Caliph
rulers.note: 'named Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi as caliph' on 29 June 2014 (Northern Iraq offensive page); the Baghuz page (2019) says he 'remained unaccounted for'. His death is not on the pages opened, so the end year is the end of the territory.

correction.text: Raqqa, 'IS controlled Raqqa from 2013', and Shaddadi (July 2013), as of 31 December 2013

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2013 (Cliopatria lacks the state; its Mujahideen row 1987-2024 is Afghan-based). April 2013: ISIL announces its expansion into Syria; Shaddadi is ISIS's from July 2013 (Al-Shaddadi page). The page gives no area for 2013. The Anbar towns of Ramadi and Fallujah are contested from 30 December 2013 (ledger), not drawn.

correction.text: the caliphate at the end of 2014: Anbar ('at least 70%'), Nineveh with Sinjar, Salah ad-Din with Tikrit and Baiji but not Samarra, Balad, Dujail and Tuz Khurmatu, western Kirkuk around Hawija; Syria's Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor governorates, the Shaddadi and al-Hawl pockets, the Manbij, Jarabulus and al-Bab districts and the Kobani canton's villages

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2014. The Salah ad-Din towns the page says ISIL did not take are cut out (Northern Iraq offensive: 'but not Tuz Khurmatu, Dujail, Balad, Samarra or Amirli'); Sinjar (August) stays in, and the June gain (ledger) excludes it so that the August gain is a real one. Anbar is drawn whole as the reading of 'at least 70%' with Ramadi half held; the 2015 Ramadi event completes the city. Area by cells about 250,000 km2 (Anbar's desert and the two Syrian governorates count in full). Infobox check: the Islamic State page has no area; the War in Iraq page says 'At its height, ISIL held 56,000 square kilometers of Iraqi territory' (the populated area) and the Military intervention page 'around 40% of Iraq at its peak in mid-2014' (about 175,000 km2), against about 193,000 km2 of Iraq in this shape (1.1 times the 40% figure, 3.5 times the 56,000 km2) and about 56,000 km2 of Syria: the shape is the governorate-sized reading, not the populated area, and the 56,000 km2 figure is the one the shape does not match. Deir ez-Zor is dated to July 2014 by the Deir ez-Zor offensive page; the Autonomous Administration dossier holds the Kobani core, the Jazira without the IS-held south and Hasakah city.

correction.text: the caliphate at the end of 2015 after Tikrit, Sinjar, Kobani, Tell Abyad, al-Hawl, the Tishrin Dam and Ramadi were lost: Syria's Raqqa (without the SDF's Tell Abyad, Ayn Issa and Tishrin discs) and Deir ez-Zor governorates, the Palmyra desert, the Manbij, Jarabulus and al-Bab districts and the Shaddadi pocket; Iraq's Anbar (without Ramadi), Nineveh without Sinjar, Salah ad-Din without Tikrit

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2015, after the losses of that year (all in the ledger). The 50% of Syria (about 92,000 km2) is the Military intervention page's figure for late May 2015; the named governorates, the Palmyra desert and the districts around Manbij, Jarabulus and al-Bab are the researcher's reading. The land held by the Autonomous Administration dossier in 2015 (Kobani canton, Tell Abyad, Ayn Issa, Tishrin, the Jazira without Shaddadi and Hasakah city) is subtracted so that the two shapes do not overlap; the 'Al Hasakah 60 km' disc of the first version is replaced by the Shaddadi pocket, the part of Hasakah ISIL held until February 2016.

correction.text: the caliphate at the end of 2016 after Ramadi, Fallujah, Shaddadi, Manbij and Jarabulus were lost: Nineveh with Mosul, Tal Afar, Hawija and Al-Qaim in western Anbar; Syria's Raqqa (without the SDF's discs) and Deir ez-Zor governorates, Palmyra (retaken 11 December), and al-Bab

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2016. The land the Autonomous Administration dossier holds in 2016 (Hasakah governorate, Manbij, Tell Abyad, Ayn Issa, Tishrin, Kobani) is subtracted. Palmyra was lost on 27 March 2016 and retaken on 11 December 2016 (ledger); al-Bab (23 February 2017) and the Iraqi towns are lost in 2017.

correction.text: the Euphrates pocket on the east bank around Hajin and Baghuz at the Iraqi border, as of 31 December 2017: 'around 5% of Syrian territory' in December 2017, of which the pocket is the part the pages draw

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2017: no territory in Iraq, none in Raqqa, Mosul, Palmyra or al-Bab. 5% of Syria is about 9,200 km2; the pocket is the 70 km disc around Abu Kamal intersected with the Deir ez-Zor east-bank polygon (about 2,300 km2), so Abu Kamal city and the west bank, which the ledger gives to Syria in November 2017, are no longer inside. The Badiya (Syrian Desert) pockets that make up the rest of the 5% are not on the pages and not drawn.

correction.text: the last pocket on the Euphrates east bank after Hajin fell on 14 December 2018: Sousa, Shafa and Baghuz Fawqani, about 4 km2 on 1 February 2019, 'only 1 square kilometer' on 12 February

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2018 and held to 23 March 2019. Hajin fell on 14 December 2018 (ledger). Drawn at its cell minimum (one cell of about 250 km2, the 25 km disc around Abu Kamal intersected with the east-bank polygon).

region.text: Raqqa, the first city under ISIL control and later its capital

ledger.note: April 2013: ISIL announces its expansion into Syria and holds Raqqa. 'The group announced expansion into Syria and renamed itself the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)' in April 2013; 'IS controlled Raqqa from 2013'; the group's headquarters at Raqqa ran 'from 2013 to 2017'.

region.text: Shaddadi and its countryside in southern Hasakah (45 km, minus Hasakah city)

ledger.note: July 2013: ISIS takes Shaddadi. The Al-Shaddadi page: 'The town was later attacked and captured by the Islamic State (ISIS) in July 2013', after a brief al-Nusra Front seizure in February 2013; the Al-Hawl offensive page calls it 'ISIL's last stronghold in the Al-Hasakah Province'. The 45 km disc is the researcher's reading of the town's district.

region.text: Anbar: Ramadi and Fallujah, then Anbar Governorate

ledger.note: 30 December 2013: war in Iraq begins at Ramadi and Fallujah. The War in Iraq page dates the war from 30 December 2013; a revolt in Ramadi 'on the eve of 2014' let ISIS gain 'control over a swath of territories in Anbar province'.

region.text: the Jarabulus and al-Bab districts on the Turkish border (35 km discs, Jarabulus minus the Kobani canton)

ledger.note: 2014: bridging. The Operation Euphrates Shield page treats the Jarabulus border strip and al-Bab as ISIL-held when the operation began on 24 August 2016, and the Manbij page dates ISIL's arrival in Manbij to January 2014; no page opened gives the capture dates of Jarabulus and al-Bab. The discs are those of the republic-of-turkey dossier's Euphrates Shield area.

region.text: the al-Hawl district in southern Hasakah (25 km disc, minus the Shaddadi pocket and Hasakah city)

ledger.note: 2014: bridging. The Al-Hawl offensive page has the SDF capturing villages 'from ISIL near Al-Hawl' in the first week of the offensive that began on 31 October 2015, and the al-Hawl town page says only that 'al-Hawl was seized by Islamic State forces' (undated). The disc is the researcher's reading; the coordinates (41.03 E, 36.38 N) are approximate, the pages opened give none.

region.text: Manbij and its pocket (al-Shahba) west of the Euphrates: 50 km, minus the Kobani canton and the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs

ledger.note: January 2014: ISIL takes Manbij from the rebels. Manbij page: 'In January 2014, forces from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) took over the city after ousting the rebels'; it had fallen to local rebel forces on 20 July 2012. The pocket is the one the Autonomous Administration dossier gains in 2016, so the two sides mirror; the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs, which the Turkish-backed rebels took, are cut out of it.

region.text: at least 70% of Anbar Governorate, with Fallujah, Al Qaim and half of Ramadi

ledger.note: June 2014: ISIL holds most of Anbar. 'By June 2014, ISIL and Baathist allies had seized at least 70% of Anbar Governorate, including Fallujah, Al Qaim, and half of Ramadi.' The whole governorate is drawn as the reading of 'at least 70%'; Ramadi is half held, so the May 2015 capture completes the city.

region.text: Mosul, Tal Afar and most of Nineveh, Tikrit and Baiji in Salah ad-Din, Hawija and western Kirkuk; not Samarra, Balad, Dujail, Tuz Khurmatu and Amirli, not Sinjar

ledger.note: June 2014: the fall of Mosul. ISIL attacked Mosul on 6 June and held it on 10 June; Tikrit on 11 June, Tal Afar on 15/16 June, the Baiji refinery on 21 June, Hawija advancing from about 8 June; 'ISIL also captured ten towns in Saladin Governorate, but not Tuz Khurmatu, Dujail, Balad, Samarra or Amirli'. Those towns are cut from the Salah ad-Din governorate (discs at Samarra, Balad-Dujail and Tuz Khurmatu, coordinates from the towns' pages), and the Sinjar disc is left for the August gain.
29 June 2014: ISIL proclaims the caliphate. 'On 29 June 2014, ISIL renamed itself the Islamic State and declared a caliphate covering Syria and Iraq', naming Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi as caliph.

region.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate on the Euphrates: Abu Kamal 1 July, Mayadin and Shuheil 3 July, the city's rebel districts 14 July

ledger.note: 1-14 July 2014: ISIS takes the Euphrates governorate from the rebels. The offensive began on 10 April 2014; 'ISIS, bolstered by reinforcements from Iraq, routed rebels from Abu Kamal after days of fighting' on 1 July; 'On 3 July, ISIS took control of the towns of Mayadin and Ash-Shuhayl'; by 14 July, when it expelled the rebels from the city, it held 95% to 98% of the governorate. The government kept part of the provincial capital, the military airport and a few towns (not subtracted).

region.text: Sinjar and the Sinjar Mountains' foot, Nineveh

ledger.note: early August 2014: Sinjar falls. 'ISIL captured the town in early August 2014'; 'ISIL captured Sinjar after the Peshmerga abandoned it'.

region.text: Raqqa Governorate outside the city, with Tabqa Air Base

ledger.note: 24 August 2014: the whole governorate. Raqqa Governorate page: 'ISIS claimed full control of this province as of August 24, 2014 when its fighters captured Tabqa Airbase'. The city was drawn from 2013 (found).

region.text: the villages of the Kobani canton, 30 km around Kobani minus the city core

ledger.note: 15 September-2 October 2014: ISIS storms the Kobani canton. 'On 15 September 2014, IS launched a massive offensive to take the Kobanî Canton and the city of Kobanî.' 'By 2 October 2014, IS succeeded in capturing 350 Kurdish villages and towns in the vicinity of Kobanê.' Around 25 September IS held 75% of the canton while the Kurds held 'only the city of Kobanî, the town of Shera, and about 15 nearby villages' (drawn as the 10 km core).

region.text: Tikrit

ledger.note: April 2015: Tikrit retaken. The Second Battle of Tikrit 'began on 2 March 2015. After more than a month of fighting, Iraqi government troops and pro-Iranian Shiite militias took the city'; the page gives no exact date.

region.text: the villages of the Kobani canton

ledger.note: 27 January 2015: Kobani is cleared. 'On 26 January, the YPG forced remaining IS fighters in Kobani to retreat'; 'The city of Kobanê was fully recaptured on 27 January'; 332 of the 350 villages were back by 17 April 2015.

region.text: Ramadi, the provincial capital of Anbar (the other half; half was held from 2014)

ledger.note: late May 2015: ISIL takes Ramadi. 'ISIL captured the provincial capital of Ramadi in late May 2015'; the War in Iraq page has it holding 'half of Ramadi' since June 2014, so the event completes a city already half held and changes the Anbar shape little (the 2014 shape draws the governorate whole).

region.text: the Palmyra desert, 150 km around Palmyra

ledger.note: late May 2015: ISIL reaches 'around 50% of Syria'. The Military intervention page gives the share and the date, not the places; the Palmyra desert is the researcher's reading of the share on top of Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor (Raqqa 17,450 and Deir ez-Zor 25,300 km2 by cells against about 92,000 km2 for half of Syria).

region.text: Tell Abyad and the corridor to Ayn Issa

ledger.note: 15-16 June 2015: Tell Abyad falls. 'Kurdish and rebel forces seized the Tell Abyad border crossing' on 15 June, 'The next day, YPG and allied forces captured Tell Abyad', linking the Kobani and Jazira cantons; Ayn Issa on 23 June (ISIL retook it on 6 July, the YPG on 8 July).

region.text: Sinjar

ledger.note: 13 November 2015: Sinjar lost to Kurdish forces. 'ISIL lost Sinjar on 13 November, to Kurdish forces'; the Peshmerga's offensive had begun on 17 December 2014.

region.text: the al-Hawl district

ledger.note: 13 November 2015: al-Hawl falls. 'On 13 November, SDF forces captured the town of Al-Hawl' in the offensive of 31 October to 30 November 2015, which took 240+ towns and villages and 2,400 km2.

region.text: Ramadi

ledger.note: 28 December 2015: Ramadi liberated. 'The Iraqi Army began its recapture campaign on 22 December. On 28 December, Iraq declared Ramadi liberated.'

region.text: the Tishrin Dam on the Euphrates

ledger.note: late December 2015: the SDF takes the Tishrin Dam and crosses the Euphrates. 'In late December 2015, the SDF captured the Tishrin Dam and crossed the Euphrates.'

region.text: Shaddadi and its countryside, southern Hasakah

ledger.note: 19 February 2016: Shaddadi falls. 'On 16 February 2016, the SDF launched an offensive to capture the strategic city of al-Shaddadi'; 'Later on 19 February, al-Shaddadi was captured by the Syrian Democratic Forces'; the offensive ended on 24 February with 315+ villages and 2,400+ km2 taken.

region.text: Palmyra and its desert

ledger.note: 27 March 2016: the Syrian Army retakes Palmyra. 'On the dawn of 27 March, the city was fully captured by the SAA after ISIL defenses collapsed' (Russian airstrikes from 9 March, ground fighting from 12 March). The page dates the city; the 150 km desert is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Fallujah

ledger.note: June 2016: Fallujah retaken. 'The Third Battle of Fallujah ended in June 2016, with the city fully liberated.'

region.text: Manbij and its pocket (50 km minus the Kobani canton and the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs)

ledger.note: 12 August 2016: Manbij falls to the SDF. The offensive began on 31 May 2016; 'On 12 August, the SDF announced that they had launched a final assault to capture the last ISIL pockets'; 'After the ISIL fighters had left, the SDF declared the city fully captured'.

region.text: Jarabulus and its border district (35 km, minus the Kobani canton)

ledger.note: 24 August 2016: Jarabulus falls. On the first day of Operation Euphrates Shield, 'Hours later, Turkish- and US-backed rebels were reported to have captured the border town of Jarabulus, with IS offering little resistance'. The rebels were Turkish-backed; the republic-of-turkey dossier draws the whole Euphrates Shield area as its occupation from 2016-08.

region.text: Palmyra and its desert

ledger.note: 11 December 2016: ISIL retakes Palmyra. The infobox of the December 2016 Palmyra offensive: 'ISIL captures Palmyra on 11 December, as well as nearby oil fields and mountains'.

region.text: Raqqa Governorate except the city: al-Thawrah and the dams

ledger.note: 2017: the SDF takes most of Raqqa governorate before the city. The Raqqa campaign, begun 6 November 2016, 'had let the SDF capture a large amount of territory in the governorate from ISIL, including al-Thawrah and the Euphrates and Mansoura dams.' The southern part (Tabqa, Resafa) is not dated by any page opened.

region.text: al-Bab and its district (35 km, minus Jarabulus)

ledger.note: 23 February 2017: al-Bab falls. 'Al-Bab was completely captured from IS by Turkish-backed rebels on 23 February.' The republic-of-turkey dossier dates its Euphrates Shield occupation to 2016-08 for the whole area.

region.text: Palmyra and its desert

ledger.note: 2 March 2017: the Syrian Army retakes Palmyra. Eastern Homs offensive page: 'On 2 March, the Syrian Army recaptured the entire city of Palmyra, after ISIL fully withdrew from the city.'

region.text: Mosul

ledger.note: 10 July 2017: Mosul retaken. 'Abadi arrived in Mosul on 9 July to announce the victory over ISIL, and an official declaration followed on 10 July'; the table gives 20 July for the Old City. The battle began on 16 October 2016.

region.text: Tal Afar and the remaining Nineveh towns

ledger.note: 20-31 August 2017: Tal Afar and the rest of Nineveh. 'The Tal Afar offensive launched on 20 August and was completed by 31 August with an Iraqi Army victory.'

region.text: Hawija, western Kirkuk

ledger.note: 5 October 2017: Hawija retaken. 'The Hawija offensive started in late September and was complete by 5 October.'

region.text: Raqqa city

ledger.note: 17 October 2017: the SDF takes Raqqa. 'The battle began on 6 June 2017. It concluded on 17 October 2017', the SDF declaring victory on 20 October.

region.text: Al-Qaim and Rawa in western Anbar (Iraqi side)

ledger.note: 17 November 2017: Al-Qaim and Rawa fall. 'Iraq captured Al-Qa'im and Rawah, ISIL's last two strongholds, on 17 November.'

region.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate north and east of the Euphrates, except the Hajin pocket

ledger.note: 8 September-25 November 2017: the SDF takes the east bank. 'The SDF launched their ground operation on 8 September 2017' to expel ISIL 'from all areas north and east of the Euphrates river'; 'SDF forces ... reached the Iraqi border on 25 November'. The Hajin pocket on the east bank stayed ISIL's until 14 December 2018. Mirrors the Autonomous Administration ledger.

region.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate west and south of the Euphrates, with Mayadin and Abu Kamal

ledger.note: September-November 2017: the Syrian Army takes the west bank. 'After ISIL lost Al-Qa'im and Abu Kamal to the Iraqi and Syrian Army, respectively', ISIL moved its capital to Hajin. The page gives no exact day for Abu Kamal; the Badiya desert pockets (the rest of the 5% of Syria ISIL held in December 2017) are not on the pages and not drawn.

region.text: Anbar, Nineveh, Salah ad-Din and western Kirkuk

ledger.note: 9 December 2017: Iraq declares victory. 'Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi announced the end of the war on 9 December'; ISIL kept hideouts in Wadi Hauran. The Military intervention page: 'no territory in Iraq, and 5% of Syrian territory' in December 2017.

region.text: Hajin and the Euphrates pocket on the east bank north-west of Abu Kamal

ledger.note: 14 December 2018: Hajin falls. The SDF's third phase began 10 September 2018; it 'fully captured Hajin as ISIL defenses collapsed' on 14 December 2018. ISIL's remaining fighters withdrew south to rural villages east of the Euphrates.

region.text: Baghuz Fawqani, about 4 km2 on 1 February 2019

ledger.note: 23 March 2019: Baghuz Fawqani falls, the last ground. 'On 23 March 2019, the SDF officially declared final victory over IS in Baghuz Fawqani'; the battle ran from 9 February; 'the territorial end of IS's self-declared caliphate'.

region.text: the last pocket at Baghuz on the Euphrates

ledger.note: 23 March 2019: the territorial Islamic State ends. 'IS lost all its territory in Syria' (infobox) and 'loses all territory in Iraq and most territory in Syria in December 2017' (Military intervention page); the group goes on as an insurgency, its Libya, Sinai and Khorasan provinces outside this map.

wars.name: War in Iraq (2013-2017)

zones.text: Anbar, Nineveh, Salah ad-Din and western Kirkuk

wars.outcome: From 30 December 2013 ISIL took Anbar's Fallujah and Ramadi, in June 2014 Mosul, Tikrit and Tal Afar; Iraqi and Kurdish forces retook Tikrit (2015), Ramadi (December 2015), Fallujah (June 2016), Mosul (10 July 2017), Tal Afar (31 August), Hawija (5 October), Al-Qaim and Rawa (17 November); Abadi announced the end on 9 December 2017.
wars.note: The page calls Kirkuk and Sinjar in October 2017 'an Iraqi-Kurdish dispute over disputed territory, not an ISIL loss'.

wars.name: Northern Iraq offensive (June 2014)

zones.text: Nineveh, Salah ad-Din, western Kirkuk and parts of Diyala

wars.outcome: 4-25 June 2014: ISIL seizes Mosul (10 June), Tikrit (11 June), Tal Afar (15-16 June) and Baiji; Kurdish forces take Kirkuk city on 13 June; the caliphate is declared on 29 June.
wars.note: The page puts the Peshmerga in Kirkuk on 13 June; Sinjar fell in early August, after the offensive.

wars.name: Siege of Kobani
wars.outcome: ISIL attacked on 15 September 2014 and took 350 villages; the YPG expelled it from the city on 26-27 January 2015 and had 332 of the 350 villages back by 17 April 2015.

wars.name: Tell Abyad offensive (2015)

zones.text: Tell Abyad, Suluk and Ayn Issa

wars.outcome: 31 May to 10 July 2015: the YPG and allies took the Tell Abyad crossing on 15 June and the town on 16 June, linking the Kobani and Jazira cantons; Ayn Issa changed hands on 23 June, 6 July and 8 July.

wars.name: Al-Hawl offensive
wars.outcome: 31 October to 30 November 2015: the SDF captured al-Hawl on 13 November and 240+ towns and villages in the offensive.

wars.name: Al-Shaddadi offensive
wars.outcome: 16 to 24 February 2016: the SDF captured Shaddadi on 19 February, 315+ villages and 2,400+ km2, ISIL's last stronghold in Hasakah.

wars.name: Manbij offensive (2016)
wars.outcome: 31 May to 12 August 2016: the SDF crossed the Euphrates, took 105 villages and farms by 14 June and Manbij city on 12 August.
wars.note: Turkey's Operation Euphrates Shield began on 24 August 2016.

wars.name: Operation Euphrates Shield
wars.outcome: 24 August 2016 to 29 March 2017: Turkish-backed rebels took Jarabulus (24 August 2016) and al-Bab (23 February 2017), 2,055 km2 and 230 settlements, ending ISIL's hold on the Turkish border.
wars.note: Turkey and its allies also clashed with the SDF over Manbij.

wars.name: Palmyra offensives (2016-2017)
wars.outcome: Syrian Army and Russian air force retook Palmyra on 27 March 2016; ISIL retook it on 11 December 2016; the Army retook it on 2 March 2017.
wars.note: The December 2016 and March 2017 dates come from the December 2016 Palmyra offensive and Eastern Homs offensive pages.

wars.name: Battle of Mosul (2016-2017)
wars.outcome: Began 16-17 October 2016; eastern Mosul declared free on 24 January 2017; the western offensive began 19 February; victory announced 9-10 July 2017, the Old City retaken by 20 July.
wars.note: By 3 December 2016 Iraqi and Peshmerga forces had retaken 5,677 km2 and 369 villages.

wars.name: Battle of Raqqa (2017)
wars.outcome: The SDF, with US airstrikes, took Raqqa between 6 June and 17 October 2017; victory declared 20 October.
wars.note: The Raqqa campaign for the governorate began on 6 November 2016 (al-Thawrah, Tabqa and Euphrates dams).

wars.name: Deir ez-Zor campaign (2017-2019)

zones.text: Deir ez-Zor Governorate, the Euphrates down to the Iraqi border

wars.outcome: The SDF opened Operation Jazeera Storm on 8 September 2017 north and east of the Euphrates; ISIL lost Al-Qa'im and Abu Kamal to the Iraqi and Syrian armies in November 2017; Hajin fell on 14 December 2018; the last pocket fell on 23 March 2019.
wars.note: The SDF said (15 September 2017) it would not let government forces cross the Euphrates, which became the dividing line.

wars.name: Battle of Baghuz Fawqani
wars.outcome: 9 February to 23 March 2019: the SDF declared final victory; IS held about 4 km2 on 1 February 2019.
wars.note: The Euphrates separates Syrian-government land from SDF land; IS militants tried to cross it on 22 April 2019.

wars.name: Military intervention against ISIL
wars.outcome: US airstrikes began in Iraq on 8 August 2014 and in Syria on 22 September 2014; IS lost all territory in Iraq and most in Syria by December 2017 and the rest on 23 March 2019.
wars.note: Share of land: 'around 40% of Iraq at its peak in mid-2014', 'around 50% of Syria by late May 2015', 'around 3% of Iraq by October 2017', '5.67% of Syria's land by November 2017'.

certainty.note: Front lines moved weekly and the pages give towns, governorates and percentages, not boundaries. The desert between towns (Anbar, the Badiya) is soft; the last pocket at Baghuz was surveyed at 4 km2 then 1 km2 (sharp in size, not in position).

sources.title: Islamic State
sources.note: Identity: April 2013 expansion, 29 June 2014 caliphate, Raqqa capital 2013-2017, 23 March 2019. Page silent on peak area, Syrian captures and most dates.

sources.title: Northern Iraq offensive (June 2014)
sources.note: The June 2014 captures: Mosul 10 June, Tikrit 11 June, Tal Afar, Baiji, Hawija; Sinjar early August; Peshmerga in Kirkuk 13 June; caliphate 29 June.

sources.title: Battle of Mosul (2016-2017)
sources.note: 16 October 2016 to 10 July 2017; 5,677 km2 retaken by 3 December 2016.

sources.title: Battle of Raqqa (2017)
sources.note: 6 June to 17 October 2017; the SDF; Raqqa the only major Syrian city fully held by ISIL in June 2017.

sources.title: Battle of Baghuz Fawqani
sources.note: 9 February to 23 March 2019; the pocket shrinking to 4 then 1 km2; the Euphrates dividing line.

sources.title: Military intervention against ISIL
sources.note: Peak shares (40% of Iraq mid-2014, 50% of Syria May 2015), 3%/5.67% in October/November 2017, airstrike dates, Libya December 2017.

sources.title: War in Iraq (2013-2017)
sources.note: The war from 30 December 2013; Anbar 70% by June 2014; Sinjar, Tikrit, Ramadi, Fallujah, Mosul, Tal Afar, Hawija, Al-Qaim dates; 9 December 2017; 56,000 km2 at its height.

sources.title: Deir ez-Zor campaign (2017-2019)
sources.note: SDF ground operation 8 September 2017; Abu Kamal and Al-Qa'im to the Iraqi and Syrian armies; the Hajin pocket, 14 December 2018; 23 March 2019.

sources.title: Siege of Kobani
sources.note: 15 September 2014 offensive, 350 villages by 2 October, 75% of the canton held around 25 September, the city cleared 27 January 2015, 332 villages back by 17 April.

sources.title: Tell Abyad offensive (2015)
sources.note: Tell Abyad crossing 15 June and town 16 June 2015; Ayn Issa 23 June, 6 and 8 July; offensive over on 10 July.

sources.title: Manbij offensive (2016)
sources.note: Tishrin Dam in late December 2015; offensive from 31 May 2016; Manbij declared captured after 12 August; Euphrates Shield from 24 August.

sources.title: Al-Hawl offensive
sources.note: 31 October-30 November 2015; al-Hawl captured on 13 November; Shaddadi 'ISIL's last stronghold in the Al-Hasakah Province'.

sources.title: Al-Shaddadi offensive (2016)
sources.note: 16-24 February 2016; Shaddadi captured on 19 February; 315+ villages and 2,400+ km2.

sources.title: Al-Shaddadi
sources.note: Captured by ISIS in July 2013 (after a brief al-Nusra seizure in February 2013); captured by the SDF on 19 February 2016.

sources.title: Manbij
sources.note: Fell to local rebels on 20 July 2012; taken by ISIL in January 2014; SDF full control on 12 August 2016; coordinates 36.528 N 37.955 E.

sources.title: Operation Euphrates Shield
sources.note: 24 August 2016 to 29 March 2017; Jarabulus captured hours after the start; al-Bab on 23 February 2017; 2,055 km2 and 230 settlements.

sources.title: Palmyra offensive (March 2016)
sources.note: Air campaign from 9 March, ground fighting from 12 March, city fully captured by the Syrian Army on 27 March 2016.

sources.title: Palmyra offensive (December 2016)
sources.note: ISIL captures Palmyra on 11 December 2016.

sources.title: Eastern Homs offensive (2017)
sources.note: 5 March-12 May 2017; the Syrian Army recaptured Palmyra on 2 March 2017.

sources.title: Deir ez-Zor offensive (April-July 2014)
sources.note: From 10 April 2014; Abu Kamal 1 July, Mayadin and Shuheil 3 July, the city's rebel districts 14 July; ISIS held 95-98% of the governorate by 14 July; a government pocket stayed in the city and the airport.

sources.title: Raqqa Governorate
sources.note: 'ISIS claimed full control of this province as of August 24, 2014 when its fighters captured Tabqa Airbase'; area 19,618 km2.

notes:
Rebel state Cliopatria lacks (its Mujahideen row 1987-2024 is owned by ia-03). New dossier by me-10-x, repaired on 2026-10-25 after review. Slugs named as counterparts by other dossiers: republic-of-iraq, kurdistan-region and autonomous-administration-of-north-and-east-syria (this batch writes the last two).

Keyframe convention of this dossier (and of the Autonomous Administration one): each keyframe is the shape as of 31 December of its first year (2018-2019: as of 31 December 2018, held to the end); land taken or lost during a year is in the ledger. The IS and AANES keyframes of 2013-2018 do not overlap (checked cell by cell); in 2019 they share only the Baghuz cell, which the SDF takes on 23 March 2019.

Repair round (review findings): (1) mirrors added for every Autonomous Administration event (Kobani 2014-09 and 2015-01, Tell Abyad and Ayn Issa 2015-06, al-Hawl 2015-11, Tishrin 2015-12, Shaddadi 2016-02, Manbij 2016-08, Raqqa governorate 2017, Deir ez-Zor east 2017-11, Hajin 2018-12, Baghuz 2019-03), with the same regions and months; (2) K2 and K3 no longer hold the SDF's land: the 'Al Hasakah 60 km' disc is replaced by the Shaddadi and al-Hawl pockets (Hasakah governorate only, minus Hasakah city); (3) the 2016 loss is split: Manbij to the Autonomous Administration (12 August), Palmyra to Syria (27 March), Jarabulus (24 August) and al-Bab (23 February 2017) to republic-of-turkey, with the Turkish-backed rebels named in the notes; Palmyra's recapture by ISIL (11 December 2016) and loss (2 March 2017) added; (4) the 2017-11 Deir ez-Zor loss is limited to the west bank, the east bank goes to the SDF except the Hajin pocket; (5) the Hajin and Baghuz regions are intersected with the east-bank polygon, so Abu Kamal city and the west bank are not in the 2017 or 2018 shapes; (6) Samarra, Balad-Dujail and Tuz Khurmatu are cut from the Salah ad-Din gain and shape (page: 'but not Tuz Khurmatu, Dujail, Balad, Samarra or Amirli'); (7) Deir ez-Zor is dated 1-14 July 2014 (Deir ez-Zor offensive page) and the rest of Raqqa governorate 24 August 2014 (Raqqa Governorate page); Manbij January 2014 and Shaddadi July 2013 are new events. Discs on the Syrian and Iraqi borders are intersected with the country, so no shape reaches into Turkey or Iraq by radius.

Where I differ from the reviewer: (a) Sinjar stays in the 2014 shape. The shape is as of 31 December 2014 and ISIL held Sinjar from early August 2014 to 13 November 2015; to make the August gain a real gain I removed Sinjar from the June gain (ledger) instead, which has the effect the reviewer asked for. (b) Ramadi: I took the reviewer's second option. The shape draws Anbar whole as the reading of 'at least 70%' (War in Iraq page: 'including Fallujah, Al Qaim, and half of Ramadi'), the May 2015 event completes a city that was half held, and the end-of-2015 shape leaves Ramadi out after 28 December. republic-of-iraq records a 2014 loss of Anbar and a December 2015 gain of Ramadi, so it needs a May 2015 loss of Ramadi (its owner's file). (c) The 2018 keyframe now covers 2018-2019 (the Baghuz pocket, as of 31 December 2018 after Hajin fell on 14 December), and the Hajin pocket is the 2017 keyframe (as of 31 December 2017); the first version had Hajin as 2018 and Baghuz as 2019.

Still not settled: the Syrian west is a reading. 'Around 50% of Syria by late May 2015' is the page's share; the Palmyra desert (150 km), the Manbij pocket (50 km, without the Kobani canton and the Euphrates Shield discs) and the Jarabulus and al-Bab discs (35 km, as in republic-of-turkey) are the researcher's discs, and the capture dates of Jarabulus and al-Bab in 2014 are on no page opened (confidence 1). The pockets in southern Hasakah (Shaddadi 45 km, al-Hawl 25 km at 41.03 E 36.38 N, approximate: no page gave coordinates) are readings; al-Hawl's seizure by ISIL is undated. The Badiya (Syrian Desert) pockets that made up the rest of the '5% of Syria' in December 2017 are not drawn. Tabqa and the southern Raqqa governorate (Syrian Army, 2017) are not dated by a page, so the whole governorate goes to the SDF at confidence 2. The government pocket in Deir ez-Zor city and the airport (2014-2017) is not subtracted. Syria's own dossier still gives Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor to ISIL in 2014 without months and Hasakah to the Autonomous Administration in 2012; its owner should align (the shapes here follow the pages).

Counterpart strings: 'syrian-opposition' (rebel-held land before ISIL took it; syria uses the same string; no dossier) and republic-of-turkey for the Turkish-backed rebels, whose Euphrates Shield occupation republic-of-turkey dates to 2016-08 for the whole area, although al-Bab fell only on 23 February 2017. Places used by radius because the gazetteer lacks them: Sinjar, Hawija (Kirkuk west), Al-Qaim, Balad-Dujail, Tuz Khurmatu, Shaddadi, al-Hawl, Jarabulus, al-Bab, Kobani, the Tishrin Dam, Hajin and Baghuz (as part of the Abu Kamal radius intersected with the east-bank polygon). Wilayat outside Iraq and Syria (Sirte, Sinai, Khorasan, West Africa) are out of scope.
